title: Akbar Administration The Dahsala System
definition: The Dahsala system, also known as the Bandobast-i-Arazi or Zabti system, was a land revenue reform introduced by Raja Todar Mal in 1580 AD to standardize revenue collection based on the average produce and prices of the preceding ten years.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the zenith of Mughal agrarian administration, frequently tested for its technical mechanisms, the role of Raja Todar Mal, and its impact on the socio-economic stability of the Mughal Empire.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Akbar Administration The Dahsala System.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Sher Shah Suri's land revenue reforms
